title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a failure in object detection or motion planning at deployment, where a system did not recognize a small animal as an obstacle requiring avoidance.

A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign. Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data and simulation replays, so it is not established whether a traffic control violation occurred. What is certain is that the autonomous system was in operation without human intervention when the collision happened.

Avride responded by restricting testing operations on certain streets and conducting experiments to improve obstacle avoidance. The incident could have been caught earlier through human monitoring of the vehicle's decisions in real-world conditions, or through testing protocols that evaluated how the system responded to small moving objects in its path.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, prompting significant community backlash. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, was familiar to residents who were upset that the self-driving car did not slow down or stop after hitting the animal. Local residents recovered the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator to preserve them.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this assertion after reviewing vehicle data and simulation replays. In response, Avride has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake. The company is now conducting controlled experiments to improve the vehicle's ability to avoid similar situations while maintaining safety performance in other scenarios.
